newsitem.title: USA: Frisch's asked to sell baseball interest.
newsitem.headline: Frisch's asked to sell baseball interest.

text.p: Two board members of Frisch's Restaurants Inc said Wednesday they have proposed the Cincinnati-based operator of the Big Boy restaurant chain sell its minority interest in the Cincinnati Reds baseball club.
The two members are both investors who last fall ousted incumbents to gain board seats.

Marge Schott, the Reds' president and chief executive officer whose colorful personality has often gained media attention, owns the largest share of the Reds although less than 50 percent, a Reds spokesman said. He said the Reds could not comment immediately on the proposal.
Frisch's management could not immediately be reached.
Investors Barry Nussbaum and Jerry Ruyan said in a statement they would like Frisch's to offer its Reds interest to Cincinnati business and civic leaders.
Nussbaum, in a telephone interview, said the eight-member Frisch's board would have to approve the sale in order for it to move forward, as would other Reds owners.
"We are hopeful the rest of the board will see what a great idea we think this is," Nussbaum said. He said the Reds investment had stopped producing a return for Frisch's.
Nussbaum said he, Ruyan and their Wolverine Partners investment firm have purchased about 8.7 percent of Frisch's since July 1996.

"Since we first announced our intention to run for the board of Frisch's, we have been very clear that we felt certain non-performing or underperforming assets needed to be sold," Nussbaum said in the statement.
